newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee regains lost ground versus dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee regains lost ground versus dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee recovered to close at 58.15 to the dollar on Wednesday in volatile trade driven by commercial demand and speculators, dealers said.

The rupee sank to 58.34 after the Central Bank pushed up the dollar by eight local cents, fixing buying and selling rates at 57.4522 and 58.6128, but later clawed back to regain lost ground, they said.
"The market was a bit volatile today because of speculators and import covering," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Speculation was spurred by dollar gains overseas and banks covering short positions ahead of the long Easter weekend, dealers said.
"The market became active and everybody started buying dollars after the Central Bank pushed the rate up by eight cents," said a local bank dealer.
The Central Bank action has more to do with the dollar's gains against the yen than the U.S. interest rate hike, which the market had factored in, said the Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Overnight call money rates remained at around 10 percent, dealers said. -- Colombo Newsroom (941) 434319
